# Glossary

One word per idea, and one place to change it: 89 terms, 23 banned phrasings.

This page is built from [`glossary.json`](../data/glossary.json): to change a word, edit the data
file and run `make glossary`. **Glossary reference in sync** fails when the page and the data disagree.

Every phrasing under **Don't say** fails **Vocabulary bans** on any prose line of any markdown file
git lists — never inside code, a fence or a link target, nor in the `solves` and `aliases` a page
keeps in other people's words. A line that must name one, as this page does, carries `<!-- vocab-ok -->`.

## Who decides a word

| Scope | Who decides |
| --- | --- |
| [Kinds](#kinds) | The content model decides the page kinds: each fixes which blocks a page carries and the folder it lives in. |
| [Blocks](#blocks) | The content model decides the blocks: each answers one question, in a fixed order per kind. |
| [Verbs](#verbs) | The relation vocabulary decides the verbs: a closed set, each paired with its inverse and declared on both pages it joins. |
| [Polarities](#polarities) | The content model decides which side of a many-sided block an item argues. |
| [Properties](#properties) | The data files and kb.mjs decide these: the facts recorded about a page beyond its frontmatter and the relation verbs — where kb.mjs files it (kind, band, group), the note on each edge in relations.json, and the roles and tours learning-paths.json gives it. The kb: names are this vocabulary's own; the built page's JSON-LD is a schema.org TechArticle (headline, description, keywords, isPartOf, author, dateModified) and carries none of them. |
| [House](#house) | The house style decides these words: the owner picks the plain word, and the ban gate fails every prose line that uses a phrasing listed under Don't say. |

## <a id="kinds"></a>Kinds

### <a id="kind-pattern"></a>pattern

- **Say:** pattern
- **Why:** A reusable solution to a recurring problem, filed at one rung of the elevation ladder or under one lens. The largest kind, and the one the other six point at.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [kb:kind](#prop-kind)

### <a id="kind-hazard"></a>hazard

- **Say:** hazard
- **Why:** A failure mode with a name — what goes wrong, what it costs, and which patterns keep it from happening. A hazard names the problem rather than fixing it; the fix is a `mitigated-by` hop away.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [mitigated-by](#verb-mitigated-by) · [exposed-to](#verb-exposed-to) · [kb:kind](#prop-kind)

### <a id="kind-theme"></a>theme

- **Say:** theme
- **Why:** A guided tour through the patterns that answer one recurring question. A theme owns its membership: its tour steps are the source of truth, and each pattern names the theme back.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [kb:kind](#prop-kind)

### <a id="kind-principle"></a>principle

- **Say:** principle
- **Why:** A design maxim — SOLID, DRY, KISS, YAGNI. Not a mechanism you build but a rule you honour, which is why it carries a mandatory block on how it fails when taken too far.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [kb:kind](#prop-kind)

### <a id="kind-design"></a>design

- **Say:** design
- **Why:** A worked case study — a system-design or low-level-design kata argued end to end, from requirements through the hard sub-problems. It joins the graph through `demonstrates`.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [demonstrates](#verb-demonstrates) · [kb:kind](#prop-kind)

### <a id="kind-capability"></a>capability

- **Say:** capability
- **Why:** One category of managed cloud service, taking the capability as its subject and the vendors' products as evidence. It joins the graph through `implements`.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [implements](#verb-implements) · [kb:kind](#prop-kind)

### <a id="kind-comparison"></a>comparison

- **Say:** comparison
- **Why:** One product decision: the managed services and open-source contenders for a single capability area, side by side, compared on the conditions that decide the choice.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [kb:kind](#prop-kind)

## <a id="blocks"></a>Blocks

### <a id="block-description"></a>description

- **Say:** description
- **Why:** Frames the subject. Its heading is kind-flavoured — “The question”, “Understanding the problem” — but the anchor is `description` on every kind, so one call fetches the opener of any page.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-explain"></a>explain

- **Say:** explain
- **Why:** One paragraph of expert-grade explanation in plain words, then one short example that shows the depth. On every kind; a design may leave it out.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [levels](#block-levels)

### <a id="block-structure"></a>structure

- **Say:** structure
- **Why:** How the happy path crosses the components, as a numbered topology walk. On an implementation pattern a sequence diagram carrying timing and the failure branches follows it; a conceptual band keeps its class-style diagram and stops there.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-variations"></a>variations

- **Say:** variations
- **Why:** The named forms the pattern takes, each a card: what changes, and what that buys.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-tradeoffs"></a>tradeoffs

- **Say:** tradeoffs
- **Why:** What the choice costs and what it buys, argued from both sides. On a design it reads as strengths against risks, biggest flaw named first.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [pro](#polarity-pro) · [con](#polarity-con)

### <a id="block-usage"></a>usage

- **Say:** usage
- **Why:** When to reach for it and when not to — the reader's situation, not the pattern's features.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [when](#polarity-when) · [avoid](#polarity-avoid)

### <a id="block-sketch"></a>sketch

- **Say:** sketch
- **Why:** The smallest code that shows the mechanism working. Collapsed by default; the language selects the highlighter.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-wild"></a>wild

- **Say:** wild
- **Why:** Real, well-known implementations that genuinely exemplify the pattern. Optional, and empty is a better answer than a guess.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-production"></a>production

- **Say:** production
- **Why:** What it takes to run: the tuning knobs, the signals to watch, what breaks first under load, and the gates before shipping.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [knob](#polarity-knob) · [signal](#polarity-signal) · [failure](#polarity-failure) · [check](#polarity-check)

### <a id="block-fluency"></a>fluency

- **Say:** fluency
- **Why:** Where the pattern shows up — the themes whose tours visit it. Hand-authored, and it must agree with the tour that owns it.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-selfcheck"></a>selfcheck

- **Say:** selfcheck
- **Why:** Three questions a reader can answer after the page, each with a short answer that links the element it rests on. Optional on a pattern, a hazard and a principle.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-causes"></a>causes

- **Say:** causes
- **Why:** What produces the hazard — the decisions and pressures that end in this failure mode.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-cost"></a>cost

- **Say:** cost
- **Why:** What the hazard costs once it lands, in the terms the person paying it feels.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-mitigation"></a>mitigation

- **Say:** mitigation
- **Why:** How to keep it from happening, as narrative. The typed edges to the patterns that prevent it live in `relationships`.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [relationships](#block-relationships)

### <a id="block-architecture"></a>architecture

- **Say:** architecture
- **Why:** The primary diagram and the walk through it. On a theme it maps a concrete system; on a design it is the board plus the trace from every functional requirement to the component that satisfies it.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-tradespace"></a>tradespace

- **Say:** tradespace
- **Why:** The axes the theme's decision moves along, and what trading one for another actually costs.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-tour"></a>tour

- **Say:** tour
- **Why:** The ordered walk through the theme's patterns, each step naming the role that pattern plays here. This is the source of truth for theme membership.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-decide"></a>decide

- **Say:** decide
- **Why:** The decision table — the conditions that pick one member of the theme over another.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-siblings"></a>siblings

- **Say:** siblings
- **Why:** The neighbouring themes, and the line where this one stops and that one starts.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-rationale"></a>rationale

- **Say:** rationale
- **Why:** Why the principle helps — the mechanism behind the maxim, not a restatement of it.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-applying"></a>applying

- **Say:** applying
- **Why:** How to honour it in practice, at the grain of a decision someone actually makes.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-overreach"></a>overreach

- **Say:** overreach
- **Why:** How it fails when taken too far. Mandatory on every principle, because a maxim with no stated limit is advice nobody can argue with.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-requirements"></a>requirements

- **Say:** requirements
- **Why:** What the system must do (functional) and how well (non-functional). Everything downstream argues from here.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-sizing"></a>sizing

- **Say:** sizing
- **Why:** Right-sizing: the interaction shape, the numbers run, and each candidate technology adopted, rejected or deferred with a reason.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-entities"></a>entities

- **Say:** entities
- **Why:** The core entities and their data design — each with its role, a one-line description and a trimmed schema.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-interface"></a>interface

- **Say:** interface
- **Why:** The API surface, grouped by caller, each endpoint with its method, path and contract.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-deepdives"></a>deepdives

- **Say:** deepdives
- **Why:** One argued deep dive per non-functional requirement, each carrying its own zoom or an iterated board.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-levels"></a>levels

- **Say:** levels
- **Why:** What a Mid, Senior and Staff candidate demonstrably does with this problem. A rubric, distinct from the `explain` block.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [explain](#block-explain)

### <a id="block-capabilities"></a>capabilities

- **Say:** capabilities
- **Why:** The provider-neutral taxonomy of what this category of service does. No product names — those are evidence, and they live in the mapping.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-mapping"></a>mapping

- **Say:** mapping
- **Why:** The cross-cloud table: each capability against what AWS, Azure and Google Cloud call it, or an honest “no first-party equivalent”.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-choosing"></a>choosing

- **Say:** choosing
- **Why:** The decision argued out — which option wins under which conditions, and why.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-portability"></a>portability

- **Say:** portability
- **Why:** What breaks when you move between providers, and what each break costs.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-contenders"></a>contenders

- **Say:** contenders
- **Why:** The products in the running, with their licenses and whether a managed offering exists.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-matrix"></a>matrix

- **Say:** matrix
- **Why:** The contenders compared on the conditions that decide the choice, one row per condition.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="block-relationships"></a>relationships

- **Say:** relationships
- **Why:** The typed edges to other pages. Generated by `kb.mjs link`, declared on both pages, and the reason the graph exists.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [mitigation](#block-mitigation)

### <a id="verb-part-of"></a>part-of

- **Say:** part-of
- **Why:** This page is one of the parts the target is built from.

### <a id="verb-prevents-hazard"></a>prevents-hazard

- **Say:** prevents-hazard — also fine: Prevents
- **Why:** Adopting this page keeps the target hazard from happening, which is why it renders as Prevents.

### <a id="verb-mitigated-by"></a>mitigated-by

## <a id="polarities"></a>Polarities

### <a id="polarity-pro"></a>pro

- **Say:** pro
- **Why:** An argument for adopting the page's subject — what it buys you.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [tradeoffs](#block-tradeoffs)

### <a id="polarity-con"></a>con

- **Say:** con
- **Why:** An argument against — what it costs, stated as a fact rather than hedged.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [tradeoffs](#block-tradeoffs)

### <a id="polarity-when"></a>when

- **Say:** when
- **Why:** A situation that calls for the pattern, written as the reader's circumstance.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [usage](#block-usage)

### <a id="polarity-avoid"></a>avoid

- **Say:** avoid
- **Why:** A situation where reaching for it makes things worse.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [usage](#block-usage)

### <a id="polarity-knob"></a>knob

- **Say:** knob
- **Why:** A configuration surface you actually turn — a named parameter, or a dial described without attributing it to a product.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [production](#block-production)

### <a id="polarity-signal"></a>signal

- **Say:** signal
- **Why:** An observable quantity worth watching: queue depth, replication lag, p99 latency.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [production](#block-production)

### <a id="polarity-failure"></a>failure

- **Say:** failure
- **Why:** What breaks first under load, and how it looks when it does.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [production](#block-production)

### <a id="polarity-check"></a>check

- **Say:** check
- **Why:** A gate to clear before shipping.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [production](#block-production)

## <a id="properties"></a>Properties

### <a id="prop-kind"></a>kb:kind

- **Say:** kb:kind
- **Why:** Which of the seven page kinds this is — `pattern`, `hazard`, `theme`, `principle`, `design` (a worked case study), `capability` (a category of managed cloud service), or `comparison` (a product decision: managed services and open-source contenders side by side).
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [pattern](#kind-pattern) · [hazard](#kind-hazard) · [theme](#kind-theme) · [principle](#kind-principle) · [design](#kind-design) · [capability](#kind-capability) · [comparison](#kind-comparison) · [kb:band](#prop-band)

### <a id="prop-band"></a>kb:band

- **Say:** kb:band
- **Why:** The band the page declares. On a pattern that is one of the thirteen elevation bands or lenses, and also its folder; on every other kind it repeats `kb:kind`, because those pages are filed by kind.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [kb:kind](#prop-kind) · [kb:group](#prop-group)

### <a id="prop-group"></a>kb:group

- **Say:** kb:group
- **Why:** The subdivision within a band, on the two bands that have one; elsewhere it repeats `kb:band`. It names the folder except where a group carries an alias and shares another's.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [kb:band](#prop-band)

### <a id="prop-note"></a>kb:note

- **Say:** kb:note
- **Why:** Why two things relate, from this side. Each side may phrase it its own way; only the edge and its verb must agree.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="prop-role"></a>kb:role

- **Say:** kb:role
- **Why:** What a pattern does in the service of one particular theme.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="prop-in-theme"></a>kb:in-theme

- **Say:** kb:in-theme
- **Why:** A theme whose tour visits this pattern. The inverse of `kb:tours`.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [kb:tours](#prop-tours)

### <a id="prop-tours"></a>kb:tours

- **Say:** kb:tours
- **Why:** A pattern this theme's tour visits. The inverse of `kb:in-theme`.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [kb:in-theme](#prop-in-theme)

### <a id="prop-tier"></a>tier

- **Say:** tier
- **Why:** Where a page sits on the way in: intro, core or advanced. Recorded in docs/data/tracks.json for every theme a Start-here track stages, never in the page's frontmatter; it orders a track and says nothing about the page's depth of reading.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

## <a id="house"></a>House

### <a id="word-use"></a>use

- **Say:** use — also fine: apply · payoff
- **Don't say:** utilise · utilize · leverage · leveraged · leveraging <!-- vocab-ok -->
- **Why:** The plain verb for putting something to work; for the noun, name the payoff itself.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="word-to"></a>to

- **Say:** to
- **Don't say:** in order to <!-- vocab-ok -->
- **Why:** Says what something is for; the longer form adds two words and nothing else.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="word-can"></a>can

- **Say:** can
- **Don't say:** demonstrates the ability to <!-- vocab-ok -->
- **Why:** Says a thing is able to do something, in one word.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="word-some"></a>some

- **Say:** some — also fine: the number itself
- **Don't say:** a number of <!-- vocab-ok -->
- **Why:** Says there are several without counting them; when you know the count, write the number instead.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="word-then"></a>then

- **Say:** then — also fine: after that · later
- **Don't say:** subsequently <!-- vocab-ok -->
- **Why:** Says what happens next, in the plain word.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="word-help"></a>help

- **Say:** help — also fine: let
- **Don't say:** facilitate · facilitated · facilitating <!-- vocab-ok -->
- **Why:** Says one thing makes another easier; say let when it makes it possible.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="word-issue"></a>issue

- **Say:** issue — also fine: generate · assign
- **Don't say:** mint · minted · minting <!-- vocab-ok -->
- **Why:** Says a system hands out a new id, key, token or number; say generate when it computes one from scratch.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei

### <a id="word-compute"></a>compute

- **Say:** compute — also fine: work out · build from · rebuild by replay
- **Don't say:** derive · deriving <!-- vocab-ok -->
- **Why:** Says a value is worked out from others; choose the word for the sense — work out, build from, or rebuild by replay.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [computed](#word-computed) · [can be worked out](#word-computable)

### <a id="word-computed"></a>computed

- **Say:** computed — also fine: worked out · built from · rebuilt by replay · generated
- **Don't say:** derived <!-- vocab-ok -->
- **Why:** Says a value was worked out from others rather than stored or typed in; choose the word for the sense.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [compute](#word-compute) · [can be worked out](#word-computable) · [subclass](#word-subclass)

### <a id="word-computable"></a>can be worked out

- **Say:** can be worked out — also fine: computable
- **Don't say:** derivable <!-- vocab-ok -->
- **Why:** Says a value follows from others, so nobody needs to store or type it.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [compute](#word-compute) · [computed](#word-computed)

### <a id="word-subclass"></a>subclass

- **Say:** subclass — also fine: child class
- **Don't say:** derived class · derived type <!-- vocab-ok -->
- **Why:** A class that extends another and inherits its members.
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei · **See:** [computed](#word-computed)

### <a id="word-software-design-atlas"></a>Software Design Atlas

- **Say:** Software Design Atlas — also fine: the Atlas · the KB
- **Don't say:** Patterns KB · patterns-kb <!-- vocab-ok -->
- **Why:** The project's name, in full at its first mention and "the Atlas" after it; "the KB" stays the plain noun for the knowledge base. An old name appears only inside a code span that records the history ([branding.md](../../.claude/rules/branding.md)).
- **Owner:** Oleksandr Derechei
